# Riemann Hypothesis / Weil Positivity — Roadmap

*Generated by pm-riemann on 2026-08-13 17:05. Manual edits will be overwritten on next sweep
— push back via OVERRIDE mail or by editing the PM config.*

**Where this stands, in one paragraph.** `paper/positivity-obstruction.tex` contains an
**unconditional** upper bound, $\limsup\mu^{-1}\log s(\mu)\le-4\pi$, a rate Connes–Consani
plot as a figure and never name. The mathematics did not move today; **the evidence under it
did.** Lean went 26 → 91 audited results and now covers Q2 and the assembly to the $-4\pi$,
not just the elementary layer; the fifteen numerical verifiers gained exit codes that can
actually fail; the paper compiles; and three CI workflows re-run all of it on a clean machine
on every push. Formalising also refuted a printed formula that four readings had missed. **The
paper's thesis is unchanged by all of it:** every one of the 91 results is sign-blind. The
prolate mechanism governs magnitude; the sign is RH; the two do not connect, and that is the
result. The open question is not throughput — it is **who outside this fleet will read it**.

## The decision I am not making

Three walls now stand between Lean and the rest of the paper, and mg-7fc6 measured each rather
than guessing:

| leg | wall | kind |
|---|---|---|
| **Q1** | a continuous branch of the Prüfer angle along an ODE-defined curve | mathlib infrastructure; the *only* chain step this blocks |
| **Q3** | Riemann–von Mangoldt, de la Vallée Poussin | missing classical analytic number theory |
| **H0** | prolate / parabolic-cylinder functions | a research library in its own right |

Building any of them is **Daniel's call, not mine.** They are not effort gaps, they are
library gaps, and the third is a multi-month project that would benefit people well outside
this repo. Until one is chosen, Q2 rests on Q1, Lemma 2.1 and Lemma 3.3, and **is not
unconditional** — precisely as mg-57a2 was scoped to expect.

## What formalising is actually buying — three for three

Every Lean run against this corpus has found a defect in **what a statement says**. None has
found an incorrect proof.

- mg-a087 — a hypothesis doing two jobs where the note named one.
- mg-7fc6 — a hypothesis omitted entirely, hiding a second external import.
- mg-57a2 — **a formula that was simply false**, copied into four places.

**The class is "the printed statement does not match the argument beneath it."** I circulated
the narrower "missing hypotheses" version this morning and mg-57a2 refuted it that afternoon.

**It has no natural detector.** In all three cases everything *derived* from the bad statement
was correct — no check failed, no number moved, nothing complained. mg-57a2's formula reached
a `CHECK` banner: an instrument quoting the wrong statement while correctly testing the right
one. That is why it is now written down (mg-83d1) rather than left in an outbox.
